stack.styling: Tailwind CSS + CSS variables for tokens
stack.primitives: hand-rolled on Radix UI (consistency with dashboard, no shadcn)
stack.motion_timeline: gsap + ScrollTrigger (one hero timeline, one cross-comparison scroll-driven)
stack.charts: visx (low-level, fully controlled) — Recharts is reserved for the dashboard

aesthetic_direction.voice: Editorial dossier. The buyer is reading a private memo prepared for them by a partner, not browsing a SaaS product. Page-turn cadence. Numbers are large and confident; prose is short and load-bearing; whitespace does the heavy lifting.
aesthetic_direction.density: low-medium. Each surface earns its scroll. No dashboards-in-a-portfolio.

headline.family: Fraunces (Google Fonts) — variable, OPSZ + SOFT + WONK axes
headline.rationale: Fraunces is a contemporary serif with a soft humanist edge — it reads as 'considered' and 'editorial' without the law-firm stiffness of Tiempos or the trend-bait of Editorial New. The variable WONK axis gives the hero a single moment of personality (subtle splay on the buyer's name) that no React/Next default ever ships with.

body.rationale: Inter Tight is dense and modern without being generic Inter. Pairing a soft serif headline with a tight neo-grotesque body is the deliberate inverse of the dashboard's all-Inter utility voice — same family root, different mood.

numeric.usage: every dollar figure, every score, every percentage in narrative copy. Tabular figures. Slightly smaller cap-height than Inter Tight so it doesn't shout next to body text.
numeric.rationale: Mono numerics in editorial layouts (NYT, FT, Bloomberg) signal 'this is a number, trust it'. In a portfolio about cash flows and scores, the typography itself becomes a credibility cue.

type_scale.usage: hero buyer name, single use per page
thesis paragraph, first paragraph of each surface

typography.weight_ladder: 400 (regular) → 500 (medium, sub-section / label) → 600 (emphasis only). 700 reserved for inline strong; no 800/900.

palette.rationale: Two-temperature palette: a deep verdant 'ledger green' anchors the brand (money, parsing, evergreen records) against a warm bone paper. Status colors are muted, not neon — this is a dossier, not a dashboard. The terracotta accent from the dashboard is intentionally NOT carried over; this app gets its own identity (gilt) so the buyer can feel the surface change.
palette.mode: dark-first (paper-on-ink), with a light 'reading mode' toggle that flips paper to ink

bone.name: Bone paper
bone.usage: primary background (light mode), primary text on ink

verdant.name: Ledger verdant
verdant.usage: surfaces, card panels in dark mode, brand accent in light

gilt.name: Antique gilt
gilt.usage: primary accent — buyer name, score numerals, hero highlight. The one warm note.

rust.name: Iron rust
rust.usage: risk / hard-gate-fail / retraction band. Muted, not alarm-red.

vellum.name: Vellum
vellum.usage: borders, dividers, low-contrast captions on bone

aesthetic_direction.motion_language: Page-turn, not slideshow. Entries ease-out at 260ms with a 12px upward translate and opacity 0→1; exits are faster (160ms, no translate) — Emil Kowalski's 'exit faster than enter' rule. Layout reorders use spring physics (stiffness 280, damping 32) — Emil's 'spring-physics on layout reorder'. Shared-element transitions on the deal-card → deal-detail navigation give the dossier its 'book-binding' feel — Emil's 'shared-element layout transitions'. No parallax. No scroll-jacking. No count-ups longer than 600ms. The R3F hero is a single contemplative drift, not a demo reel. Everything clamps to opacity-only under prefers-reduced-motion.
ui_pro_max_rules_applied: Accessibility-first (priority 1): WCAG 2.2 AA on every surface; AAA on body text
Touch (priority 2): 44x44 hit targets minimum, 48x48 on the three deal cards
Performance (priority 3): R3F lazy-loaded, single hero scene, <10k tris budget
Style (priority 4): one accent color (gilt) used sparingly — under 5% of surface
Type (priority 6): max two type families + one mono; modular scale documented
Color (priority 6): non-load-bearing semantic colors (status always has icon + word)
Animation (priority 7): durations clamped, prefers-reduced-motion respected, no decorative loops

surfaces.purpose: Establish the buyer as the narrative protagonist and the document as a designed artifact, not a SaaS page
surfaces.content: Buyer name (set in Fraunces display, WONK axis nudged), one-sentence thesis, as_of_date, single R3F scene (slow-drifting ledger / cards / paper), CTA: 'Begin reading'
surfaces.motion_role: GSAP entry timeline orchestrates: 0ms type-mask reveal of buyer name (letters drawn) → 700ms R3F scene fades in → 1200ms thesis line types-on → 1800ms CTA fades in. Single timeline, scrubable for reduced-motion (jump-to-end).

surfaces.purpose: Articulate the buyer's posture: capital, operator profile, what they're hunting and why
surfaces.content: Editorial layout. Left column: prose ('22, six months at Big 4, lives at home, $22k liquid, $450k SBA capacity, twelve hours a week — the constraints are the strategy'). Right column: pull-quote with the target_owner_profit number set in gilt JetBrains Mono at display size.
surfaces.motion_role: Motion fade-up on scroll-into-view (260ms, ease-out). Shared-element transition on the buyer-name from hero (Emil pattern).

surfaces.purpose: The honest pivot. Tell the buyer: zero clean wins today, here's what we found, here's why that's information not failure
surfaces.content: Three large blocks: 'Negotiable' (L002), 'Future-target' (L003), 'Flagged' (L004). Each block is one paragraph of prose + one Rive fit-gauge (score / 100). This surface frames everything that follows. The framing line — 'Three listings. Zero clean wins. One conversation worth having today.' — is the load-bearing copy of the entire portfolio.
surfaces.motion_role: Motion stagger (40ms between blocks, 260ms each). Rive gauges run their entry state machine on intersection-observer trigger.

surfaces.purpose: Present the negotiable candidate with full color: why it's the one to call about, where the gap is, what the conversation looks like
surfaces.content: Cover (business name, score 62, location, asking $360k, EBITDA $107k vs target $140k — set side-by-side, gilt). Sub-sections: 'Why it's the one to talk about', 'The $33k gap (and how negotiation closes it)', 'Top 5 risks' (Rive risk-meter), 'Top 5 opportunities', 'What the broker isn't saying' (the franchisor identity hidden), 'Recommended ask: NDA + price negotiation to $300k OR seller note', 'Receipts' (link to DD appendix anchor).
surfaces.motion_role: Per-card Rive gauge for fit-score (animated arc, state machine: enter / fail / pass / negotiable). Motion layout transition from /findings card to full /deals/l002 page (shared-element). Subtle GSAP scroll-pin on the $33k gap visualization — a single moment, not a sequence.

surfaces.purpose: Present L003 as the right business at the wrong moment. Establish the 18-24 month patience play.
surfaces.content: Cover (FedEx P&D Routes, score 44, asking $525k, SDE $162k). Headline: 'The right model. The wrong moment.' Sub-sections: 'Why this is the dream model' (true absentee, protected territories, manager in place), 'Why it cannot happen today' ($350k min down vs $22k liquid, SBA explicitly blocked), 'The 18-24 month math' (small Sankey: consulting income → savings rate → liquid capital trajectory), 'What to watch' (FedEx ISP program changes, similar listings to monitor).
surfaces.motion_role: Motion fade-up. Sankey draws progressively on scroll (Motion path-length animation, not GSAP — single chart, no need for timeline). Rive gauge encodes 'gated' state distinctly from L002's 'negotiable' state.

surfaces.purpose: System-integrity moment. Show the buyer the deal that LOOKED too good and explain how the filter caught it. This is the credibility surface.
surfaces.content: Cover band in rust (subdued, not alarm). Title: 'L004 — Savannah Gasket Replacement.' Sub-headline: 'Looked like a 94% first-year return. Wasn't.' Sections: 'The original case' (1.07x SDE multiple, $294k CF on $315k ask, the math that seduced a faster system), 'The geography reject' (Savannah is 4 hours from Atlanta — operator-fit fail), 'The pattern that emerged' (Donald Webster broker pattern: 4+ listings under 1.5x SDE across pest control, aircraft detailing, fencing, gasket replacement — same broker, same anomaly, different industries). 'Why we surface this' (the filter only works if you can see what it caught).
surfaces.motion_role: Rust band fades in on enter (Motion, 320ms — slightly slower than other entries to land the weight). The broker-pattern reveal uses a small Lottie of dots clustering into a flagged ring (single-use, decorative-but-meaningful — under 40KB).

surfaces.purpose: Multi-axis view of L002 vs L003 vs L004 across the dimensions the buyer cares about
surfaces.content: Three axes revealed sequentially on scroll: (1) price vs first-year cash yield to buyer, (2) operator-fit vs effort required, (3) capital-feasibility today vs in 24 months. Each axis is a visx scatter / dot-plot with deal labels in JetBrains Mono.
surfaces.motion_role: GSAP ScrollTrigger drives the axis-by-axis reveal. Each axis: ink-line draws across screen (700ms), then deal-dots settle into position (Motion spring, 320ms each, staggered 80ms). Three axes total, one sequence. This is the second of two GSAP uses in the whole app.

surfaces.purpose: Convert the dossier into action. Three concrete tasks, in order.
surfaces.content: Numbered list, large type, generous whitespace. 1. 'Call Mark Werbalowsky at Sunbelt Atlanta about L002. Ask for the franchisor name, FDD Item 19, and whether seller will accept $300k or carry a note.' 2. 'Open a savings account discipline now. L003 needs $350k. Eighteen months of consulting bonuses + side-saving can get you there.' 3. 'Pre-qualify with an SBA preferred lender. Six months of W-2 + a clear narrative beats waiting two years.' Each step has an estimated-time chip and the exact source citation underneath.
surfaces.motion_role: Motion crossfade between an at-rest and on-hover state for each step (the step number fills with gilt on hover). No timeline.

surfaces.purpose: The 'why trust this output' surface. A one-page accounting of what the system rejected and why.
surfaces.content: Timeline-style list (vertical, ink-rule down center): L004 retroactively flagged → broker-pattern hardened in rubric → L007/L008 retracted → search-rubric-buyer-001.md updated. Each event has date, agent, outcome, and a one-line takeaway. This is the surface that says 'the negative results are part of the product.'
surfaces.motion_role: Motion stagger on scroll (60ms between events, 240ms each). No GSAP needed.

surfaces.purpose: The receipts. Full DD packets behind accordion expand. This is the 'show your work' surface.
surfaces.content: Three accordion panels, one per deal. Each expanded panel renders the DD claims list (with source URLs, retrieved_at, confidence scores), red flags, follow-up actions. Plain typography, no decoration — this surface intentionally looks like a printed appendix.
surfaces.motion_role: dotLottie expand/collapse glyph (small, 24x24, 12KB). Motion height-animation on accordion content (200ms ease-out, instant on prefers-reduced-motion). sr-only text always present (open/close state announced).

scenes.depicts: Three suspended paper cards (representing the three deals) drifting in a slow ambient rotation under a single warm rim-light. Cards are blank rectangles with a subtle gilt edge — the buyer's eye fills in the meaning. No text in the 3D scene. Camera is fixed; scene drifts.
scenes.loading: next/dynamic with ssr:false, Suspense fallback = static PNG at same camera angle (2x DPR, < 80KB AVIF)
scenes.prefers_reduced_motion: render the static PNG fallback, do not mount the canvas
scenes.mobile: static PNG fallback under 768px viewport (R3F skipped on mobile to preserve INP)
scenes.asset_source: primitives only (BoxGeometry rounded via drei <RoundedBox>), no external GLB

timelines.behavior: Letter-mask reveal of buyer name → R3F fade-in → thesis type-on → CTA fade-in
timelines.why_gsap_not_motion: Sequence of dependent steps with precise timing across heterogeneous elements (SVG mask, canvas, DOM). GSAP timeline syntax is cleaner than chained Motion variants. Single use justified.
timelines.prefers_reduced_motion: timeline.progress(1) on mount — all elements snap to final state

timelines.behavior: Three axes revealed sequentially as user scrolls through pinned viewport
timelines.why_gsap_not_motion: ScrollTrigger pin + scrub-driven reveal across three sub-scenes is GSAP's home turf. Motion's scroll utilities are less ergonomic for pin behavior.
timelines.prefers_reduced_motion: ScrollTrigger disabled; all three axes render at full opacity simultaneously, scroll behaves normally (no pin)

gsap.rule: GSAP appears in exactly two surfaces. Everywhere else, Motion.

motion.prefers_reduced_motion: All translate values → 0. All durations → 1ms (effectively instant). Opacity transitions preserved at half duration (no motion sickness risk from pure opacity).

files.purpose: Score / 100 arc gauge used on every deal card (3 instances)
states: gated (L003, 44/100 → moss arc with rust gate-icon)
flagged (L004, n/a → rust arc with strike-through)
files.source: custom — produced ahead of build in Rive editor (rive.app)
files.fallback: static SVG at same dimensions; sr-only text 'Fit score: 62 of 100 — negotiable'
static SVG, sr-only text with numeric

rive.rule: Rive only where the asset encodes state transitions a static SVG cannot. Never decorative.

files.purpose: Dots clustering into a flagged ring on /deals/l004 — visual metaphor for the broker pattern discovery
files.source: custom dotLottie (.lottie format, not raw .json — 60% smaller)
files.fallback: static SVG of the final clustered state
CSS rotate on a static SVG chevron

asset_pipeline.notes: Primitives only; no external GLB. Render fallback PNG first via headless render or single screenshot from dev.

asset_pipeline.owner: portfolio-designer (designs state machine) or human (if Rive editor preferred locally)
asset_pipeline.notes: Must exist before /findings and /deals/[id] surfaces are buildable. Static SVG fallback in same directory.

asset_pipeline.owner: portfolio-designer (can be produced last; surface renders without it)

asset_pipeline.alternative: Pure CSS rotate on inline SVG — if Lottie file slips, ship CSS

asset_pipeline.deliverable: apps/portfolio/src/app/fonts.ts using next/font/google for Fraunces + Inter Tight + JetBrains Mono
asset_pipeline.subsetting: Latin only; preload Fraunces display weight + Inter Tight 400/500

asset_pipeline.deliverable: NONE in v1 — surfaces are typography + R3F + Rive + Lottie + visx. No stock photography. No illustration.
asset_pipeline.rationale: Editorial design pattern: when typography and motion carry the design, photography becomes a distraction. Deferred to v2 if needed.

accessibility_notes: WCAG 2.2 AA on every surface; AAA on body text contrast (ratios documented in palette.contrast_table). [ui-ux-pro-max rule 1: Accessibility-first]
Touch targets minimum 44x44 px (WCAG 2.5.5); 48x48 on the three primary deal cards. [ui-ux-pro-max rule 2: Touch]

Color is never load-bearing. Score arcs include numeric text. Status colors (rust/moss/gilt) always paired with icon + word. Hard-gate badges show ✓/✗ icon + 'PASS'/'FAIL' string. [ui-ux-pro-max rule 6: Color]

prefers-reduced-motion: all translate animations → 0px, durations → 1ms (functionally instant), R3F replaced by static PNG, GSAP timelines progress(1) on mount, Lottie replaced by static SVG. [ui-ux-pro-max rule 7: Animation]
Keyboard navigation: skip-to-main link first on every page, Tab order follows DOM order, focus-visible rings always rendered (2px gilt ring + 2px ink offset, never outline:none without replacement)
Headings: one h1 per route, h2 for sections, h3 for cards, no level skips
Page titles follow '<Surface> — Buyer 001 Dossier' for scannable browser history
R3F canvas marked aria-hidden=true; the hero's narrative meaning is conveyed by surrounding text — the 3D is atmosphere
Rive gauges include sr-only text with the numeric value and state name (e.g., 'Fit score: 62 of 100 — negotiable')
Lottie containers marked aria-hidden=true; meaning is in surrounding copy
visx charts in /comparison include sr-only data tables mirroring scatter data (same a11y pattern dashboard used for Recharts)
Color contrast verified at AA minimum for all foreground/background pairs; documented in palette.contrast_table
Light/dark mode toggle is keyboard-reachable, announces state via aria-pressed, respects system preference on first load
Reading mode (light) defaults to system; user choice persisted to localStorage with no-flash inline script in <head>
Forms / inputs: none in v1 (read-only dossier). When added in v2, follow ui-ux-pro-max forms rules (label association, error text via aria-describedby, autocomplete tokens)
Charts (visx): every scatter point keyboard-focusable, tooltips reachable via Tab + Enter, sr-only data table provides parity
system_integrity_moments: the-three-truths surface opens with 'Three listings. Zero clean wins.' — sets honesty as the framing before any deal is presented
/deals/l004 (Flagged) shows the broker-pattern discovery in the portfolio itself — the system surfaces what it filtered out, not just what survived
/system appendix lays out the L007/L008 retractions and broker-pattern hardening with dates and outcomes — the negative results are part of the product
build_sequence_for_portfolio_designer: 1. Scaffold apps/portfolio/ (Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript strict, Tailwind). Mirror dashboard's hand-rolled-on-Radix posture; do not install shadcn.
2. Token layer: globals.css with the 7 palette CSS variables + dark/light flip + type-scale rem tokens.
3. Typography: next/font/google for Fraunces + Inter Tight + JetBrains Mono, latin-only subset, Fraunces variable axes enabled.
4. Vault read layer: server-only utilities to parse the 3 listing files + 3 assessment files + 3 DD/memo files + buyer profile + search rubric. Typed against SCHEMAS.md.
5. Primitives: Button, Card, Accordion (Radix), FocusRing, ReadingModeToggle, ReducedMotionProvider, ScrollLink.
6. Status atoms: ScoreBadge, HardGateBadge, ConfidenceMeter (these are visually distinct from the dashboard's — different palette, different typography, same a11y contract).
7. Build /hero LAST (R3F + GSAP timeline) — build with static PNG fallback first, layer R3F on top.
8. Build /thesis — typography-driven, no motion library needed yet.
9. Build /findings (the-three-truths) — first surface that mounts Rive. Ship with static SVG fallback; swap in Rive once .riv files exist.
10. Build /deals/[id] for L002, L003, L004 in that order. Shared-element transition from /findings card.
11. Build /comparison — visx scatter + GSAP ScrollTrigger pin. Second and final GSAP use.
13. Build /system — Motion stagger timeline of events.
14. Build /appendix — accordion + dotLottie chevron + sr-only data tables for DD claims.
15. Build /hero — R3F scene (last; can ship with static PNG and add 3D iteratively).
16. A11y pass: keyboard walkthrough every surface, axe-core CI, screen-reader pass on /findings + /deals/[id] + /comparison + /appendix.
17. Reduced-motion pass: flip OS setting, walk every surface. R3F replaced by PNG. GSAP snaps. Lottie replaced by SVG.

18. Performance pass: Lighthouse on every route. Target: Performance ≥ 90 on /thesis, /findings, /next-steps, /system, /appendix. Performance ≥ 75 on /hero, /comparison, /deals/[id] (R3F and GSAP-pin surfaces have a budget hit; documented and intentional).

19. GATE 5 checklist: every surface has prefers-reduced-motion fallback, no decorative loops, no scroll-jacking, all 3 deals render from vault data (no hardcoded numbers), R3F lazy-loaded (verified in network panel), shared-element transitions work both directions.
open_questions_for_orchestrator: Should /comparison include a fourth deal-slot for 'placeholder — a future fit lives here'? Argues for: forward-looking narrative, sets reader expectation. Argues against: dilutes the honesty of 'three listings, zero clean wins'.
Reading mode default: dark-first (paper-on-ink, dramatic) or light-first (paper-on-bone, classical)? Recommendation: dark-first to differentiate from dashboard's neutral-slate light-first.
Does the buyer want a printable/PDF export of the dossier? Editorial layout makes print plausible. Recommendation: defer to v2; the surface is web-first.

Where does the Rive editing happen — portfolio-designer authors .riv files via Rive's web editor (free tier), or does the human want to author them? Recommendation: portfolio-designer authors, human reviews before commit.

Confirm that /portfolio is reachable from the dashboard's GlobalNav (the dashboard plan stubs an external link). Should the link open in a new tab or same tab? Recommendation: new tab — the dossier is a 'destination', not a sub-page.
Skill availability: ui-ux-pro-max CLI is broken (RN-biased + symlinks); SKILL.md was used as static reference. Confirm orchestrator is OK with that pre-flight call before portfolio-designer starts.
